sources.name: Ray Dalio · Economic Principles
sources.watch: Debt service versus income; credit creation; deleveraging mechanisms; domestic versus foreign-currency debt.
sources.limits: Conceptual framework, not an official real-time stage classification.

sources.name: Bridgewater Associates
sources.access: Selected public research; institutional research is not all public
sources.watch: Growth and inflation surprises, policy constraints, liquidity and portfolio sensitivities.
sources.limits: The dashboard is independent and is not a Bridgewater forecast or endorsement.

sources.name: J.P. Morgan Global Research
sources.access: Public summaries; full research may require client access
sources.watch: Global growth, rates, credit spreads and earnings revisions.
sources.limits: Distinguish published research from a bank's positioning or sales commentary.

sources.name: Goldman Sachs Insights
sources.access: Public insights; some research is client-only
sources.watch: Growth, inflation, financial conditions, commodity supply and demand.
sources.limits: Read publication dates and assumptions; forecasts can disagree.

sources.name: Morgan Stanley Insights
sources.access: Public summaries; full reports may require access
sources.watch: Macro outlook, policy, equity earnings and cross-asset strategy.
sources.limits: Equity earnings are a useful cross-check, not a debt-cycle measure by themselves.

sources.name: Bank of America Institute
sources.watch: Consumer spending, household cash flow and business activity.
sources.limits: Bank customer samples are not the entire economy.

sources.name: Citi GPS
sources.access: Selected public reports; other research requires access
sources.watch: Structural risks, global growth, technology and debt sustainability.
sources.limits: Long-horizon themes need separate evidence for near-term market effects.

sources.name: UBS Chief Investment Office
sources.access: Public outlooks; access varies by report
sources.watch: Base, upside and downside scenarios; rates, currencies and earnings.
sources.limits: Separate conditional scenarios from high-conviction predictions.

sources.name: Deutsche Bank Research
sources.watch: Credit conditions, fiscal policy and regional economic cycles.
sources.limits: Check geographic coverage before applying a conclusion to the US.

sources.name: HSBC Global Research
sources.watch: Global trade, emerging markets, currencies and international credit.
sources.limits: Listed as a reading source; paywalled text is not scraped.

sources.name: The Economist · Finance & economics
sources.watch: Debt, productivity, monetary policy and historical comparisons.
sources.limits: Journalistic interpretation; trace important claims to primary data.

sources.name: Financial Times · Global economy
sources.watch: Fiscal credibility, bond markets, banks and international policy.
sources.limits: News and opinion are different evidence types.

sources.name: Reuters · Markets
sources.access: Access varies by region and article
sources.watch: Dated policy decisions, market reactions and attributed statements.
sources.limits: A market move after an event does not establish a causal effect.

sources.name: IMF · Global Financial Stability Report
sources.watch: Leverage, refinancing, sovereign and financial-sector vulnerabilities.
sources.limits: Publication lag and scenario assumptions matter.

sources.name: BIS · Quarterly Review
sources.watch: Private-sector credit, debt-service ratios and cross-border funding.
sources.limits: Credit aggregates have coverage differences and release lags.

sources.name: Federal Reserve · Financial Stability Report
sources.watch: Valuations, business and household borrowing, leverage and funding risks.
sources.limits: Financial vulnerability is not a prediction of a crisis date.

sources.name: New York Fed · Household Debt and Credit
sources.watch: Delinquencies, household credit growth and repayment pressure.
sources.limits: Households are only one part of a country's debt cycle.

sources.name: Congressional Budget Office
sources.watch: Government interest costs, deficits and long-term debt projections.
sources.limits: Government debt alone does not identify private-sector deleveraging.
